programs.title: Woman at the end of the world
programs.desc: This season was special in many ways.It included the 100th anniversary episode, produced for the first time in Poland.At the same time, this series was considered the most difficult, because due to the pandemic, Martyna Wojciechowska had to stay in the country for four months, and further photos might not have been taken at all.However, for both the traveler and her heroines, the impossible does not exist.In the last episode, viewers will learn about the behind-the-scenes of the program, prepared during the pandemic.Despite the border closure, the team traveled a distance equal to one length of the equator, meeting truly extraordinary women.

programs.title: Woman at the end of the world
programs.desc: The Roma live in most countries, but do not have their own country.According to estimates, there are from 8 to 15 million of them in the world, and in Romania - from about 500,000 to 2 million.Among the many Roma communities are the Gabors, who traditionally have the same surname to honor the Hungarian king from whom they received rights in the 17th century.They are referred to as aristocracy due to their light skin and financial status.They are distinguished by their attachment to tradition and the Adventist church.Men wear hats and mustaches.If they do not have the latter, it means that they have renounced their origins.Women, on the other hand, must hide their hair from marriage until death, and cannot wear makeup, lipstick or long nails.Their beauty lies in their naturalness.Although individual families traditionally pursue specific professions, they run the home.Martyna Wojciechowska, however, meets Rosalina in Transylvania, who is learning crafts in her future father-in-law's workshop.

programs.title: Woman at the end of the world
programs.desc: Saudi Arabia is one of the few absolute monarchies in the world where Muslim Sharia law still applies.Raha Moharrak was born there - she had enough courage and determination to break the prevailing patterns, thanks to which she was able to fulfill her dreams and conquer the Crown of the Earth, the highest peaks of seven continents.The heroine of the episode achieved this as the first woman from Saudi Arabia.In a country where her gender gained voting rights only in 2011, and in 2018 they were allowed to drive a car or travel abroad without the consent of a male guardian.The biggest problem for Raha was getting her father's consent to participate in the Kilimanjaro expedition, because according to Sharia law, a daughter must obey her parent, and he was against her idea, as was traditional society.However, the girl did not give up.When she conquered Mount Everest, she became a national media star.She continues to inspire other women.

programs.title: Man vs World
programs.desc: Rob Bell, an adventurer, athlete and engineer, sets off on a journey during which he will travel only in vehicles powered by human muscles.Every morning the traveler will take on a new challenge.Wanting to visit as many places as possible and reach the destination before sunset, he will learn about disciplines such as canyoning, paragliding, mountain biking, mountain kayaking, coasteering and mountainboarding.During the expedition, he will cover difficult areas of South Africa, Poland, the Czech Republic and Great Britain.He will also meet many guides who will give him advice on how to navigate the cliffs, slopes and river gorges.When Rob undergoes this endurance test, he will see the world from a completely new perspective.
